messages:
maria: Hey team — customer reported a bunch of client timeouts around 12:23 UTC (502 responses). Can someone point me to the shortest path to collect evidence (dashboards, query snippets, and a trace sample) so I can attach to the support ticket? I can triage but need the exact panels/queries. :eyes:

ajay: Short path: Grafana -> Ingress -> 'requests by status' panel. Also check 'upstream latency p95' and 'gateway queue depth'. Links: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/abcd123/ingress-overview and https://grafana.redwood.company/d/efgh456/upstream-latency

ajay: Quick logs query for 502s in Loki: 
```
{job="ingress"} | json | status_code=~"5\\d{2}" | status_code=502 | line_format "{time} {path} {upstream_host} {request_id}"
```

ajay: And a simple metric query (Prometheus): 
```
sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="ingress",status=~"5.."}[5m])) by (route)
```

lina: For traces, use the trace id from the ingress logs field `request_id`. If you have a request_id, in Jaeger: `service=ingress`, `tags.request_id=<id>` then look for spans around the same timestamp. Sample filter: `operation =~ " .*handleRequest.*" and duration>200ms and error=true`

lina: If this is a short burst, our alert has historically been noisy. If you want to propose a quick adjustment for the on-call alert, two low-effort options: 1) increase evaluation window to 5m (from 1m) or 2) add a minimum count threshold (e.g., only fire if >10 5xx in 2m). Which channel is this ticket?

maria: Ticket is SUP-1129 (customer-facing). I can try the Loki query now. Can someone paste the exact curl to get a trace link if I have a request_id?

phil: curl to get trace id from the trace API (internal): 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TRACE_TOKEN" "https://tracing.redwood.company/api/traces?service=ingress&tag=request_id:%3CREQUEST_ID%3E"
```

phil: Or use the Jaeger UI shortcut: https://tracing.redwood.company/jaeger/search?service=ingress&tags=request_id%3D<REQUEST_ID>

sre-bot: [runbook] 502/gateway-timeout triage checklist posted: https://wiki.redwood.company/runbooks/502-triage (automated)

maria: Ran the Loki query, pulled 6 hits, paths mostly `/v1/generate` and `/v1/chat`. Upstream_host shows `backend-pool-a` for 4, `backend-pool-b` for 2. request_ids: r-8f7a, r-8f7b, r-8f7c, r-8f7d, r-8f7e, r-8f7f.

lina: Good, filter traces for r-8f7a first. If backend-pool-a has multiple 502s and p95 upstream latency > 300ms, likely backend overload. Check retry rate and 429s on the backend too.

ajay: Also check the gateway queue metric: `ingress_queue_depth` by node around 12:20-12:25. If queue spikes then it's probable we hit connection limits. Query: `max_over_time(ingress_queue_depth[5m])`

phil: For a quick SLO/alert change suggestion: SUP-1129 is customer-impacting so we probably leave the main alert as-is but add a temporary suppression rule for <3min bursts. For longer term, we want to switch to a percentile-based alert (p99 5xx rate) + count threshold.

maria: Thanks — I have traces for r-8f7a and r-8f7b. Both show a TCP connection reset from the upstream host at the time of the error. Attaching one screenshot to the ticket. I'll propose: increase alert eval window to 5m and add count>8 in 2m as a follow-up PR.

lina: Sounds good. For PR, ping `#eng-sre` and reference runbook link. Also cc product on the customer impact note.

maria: Will do. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

phil: If you want I can open a small changelist to add the temporary debounce today (2 lines in the alert config).

maria: That'd be great — if you can link the PR here I'll merge after QA.

phil: PR: https://git.redwood.company/alerts/merge_requests/278 — adds `min_count: 8` and `eval_window: 5m` (temporary).

maria: Merged and noted in SUP-1129. Closing this loop. Appreciate the quick help.
